questions.q: A CAPTCHA tells a real person from a programme. What does the editorial say life’s hardships tell apart in the same way?
options: The sincere person, who meets difficulty with patience and positive planning, from the insincere, who reacts impatiently
Yes. Hardship is life’s challenge-response test.
The rich from the poor
Not quite. The article says: The sincere person, who meets difficulty with patience and positive planning, from the insincere, who reacts impatiently.
The learned from the unlearned
Not quite. The article says: The sincere person, who meets difficulty with patience and positive planning, from the insincere, who reacts impatiently.

questions.q: “God is great” is an obvious truth. What does the article say is the other half that must be grasped with it?
options: That greatness can be earned
Not quite. The article says: That man himself is small – only then does the first truth produce humility.
That other people are small
Not quite. The article says: That man himself is small – only then does the first truth produce humility.
That man himself is small – only then does the first truth produce humility
Right. Every truth is a half-truth until one sees how it applies to oneself.
That the universe is small
Not quite. The article says: That man himself is small – only then does the first truth produce humility.
questions.rationale: “To utter the words, ‘God is great’ is to acknowledge an outward reality, and to say, as a corollary, ‘I am small,’ indicates one’s willingness to mould oneself to this outer reality.”

options: Fasting is unconnected with the Quran

Not quite. The article says: The Quran is the reward from God, and fasting is the grateful acknowledgment of it.

Not quite. The article says: The Quran is the reward from God, and fasting is the grateful acknowledgment of it.

questions.q: A celebrated writer received a great literary award seventy years after his first book. What was his response?
options: “I owe this to my readers”
Not quite. The article says: “I am too old to be happy”.
“This is the beginning of my work”
Not quite. The article says: “I am too old to be happy”.

Not quite. The article says: “I am too old to be happy”.

questions.rationale: “‘I am too old to be happy,’ he said.”

Yes. It is people who make history, not resources.
A house full of books
Not quite. The article says: A house full of men of sound character, like three Companions he named.
A house full of grain for the poor
Not quite. The article says: A house full of men of sound character, like three Companions he named.

Not quite. The article says: A house full of men of sound character, like three Companions he named.
questions.rationale: “My greatest wish, on the contrary, would be to have this house full of men like Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah, Muadh ibn Jabal and Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman.”
